---
title: "The Infrastructure Zoo"
subtitle: "Regional Grids and Sustainability Baselines"
---

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: false
import mlsysim

_grids = mlsysim.Infrastructure.Grids
_quebec = _grids.Quebec
_poland = _grids.Poland
_ci_quebec = _quebec.carbon_intensity_g_kwh
_ci_poland = _poland.carbon_intensity_g_kwh
_ci_ratio = _ci_poland / _ci_quebec
_pue_quebec = _quebec.pue
_pue_poland = _poland.pue
_ovh_quebec = (_pue_quebec - 1.0) * 100
_ovh_poland = (_pue_poland - 1.0) * 100
```

The Infrastructure Zoo provides the **Environmental Context** for ML deployments: the carbon intensity
of regional electricity grids and datacenter efficiency profiles. Every value is sourced from
published government energy data and IEA reporting.

::: {.callout-important}
## Carbon Intensity Varies `{python} f"{_ci_ratio:.0f}×"` Across Registered Regions
Training the same model in Quebec (hydro-dominated, `{python} f"{_ci_quebec:.0f} gCO₂/kWh"`) vs. Poland (coal-dominated,
`{python} f"{_ci_poland:.0f} gCO₂/kWh"`) differs by **`{python} f"{_ci_ratio:.0f}×"`** in grid carbon intensity (`{python} f"{(_ci_poland * _pue_poland) / (_ci_quebec * _pue_quebec):.1f}×"` after PUE). Use the [Geography Tutorial](../tutorials/07_geography.qmd)
to explore these tradeoffs interactively.
:::

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
def print_grid_table(title, grid_class):
    print(f"### {title}")
    print("| Region | Carbon Intensity | Typical PUE | Primary Source |")
    print("|:---|:---:|:---:|:---:|")

    for attr_name in sorted(dir(grid_class)):
        if attr_name.startswith("_"): continue
        item = getattr(grid_class, attr_name)
        if "GridProfile" in type(item).__name__:
            print(f"| **{item.name}** | {item.carbon_intensity_g_kwh} gCO2/kWh | {item.pue} | {item.primary_source.capitalize()} |")
    print("\n")

def print_rack_table(title, rack_class):
    print(f"### {title}")
    print("| Rack Class | Power Density | Cooling Type |")
    print("|:---|:---:|:---:|")

    for attr_name in sorted(dir(rack_class)):
        if attr_name.startswith("_"): continue
        item = getattr(rack_class, attr_name)
        if "RackProfile" in type(item).__name__:
            print(f"| **{item.name}** | {item.power_kw} kW | {item.cooling_type.capitalize()} |")
    print("\n")

reg = getattr(mlsysim, "Infrastructure", None)
if reg:
    if hasattr(reg, "Grids"):
        print_grid_table("Regional Electricity Grids", reg.Grids)
    if hasattr(reg, "Racks"):
        print_rack_table("Datacenter Rack Profiles", reg.Racks)
else:
    print("Error: Infrastructure registry not found in mlsysim.")
```

---

## How to Read the Infrastructure Zoo

### Carbon Intensity: The Biggest Lever

The single most impactful decision for ML sustainability is **where** a model is trained. Carbon intensity varies by `{python} f"{_ci_ratio:.0f}×"` across the grids above. Quebec's hydro-dominated grid produces `{python} f"{_ci_quebec:.0f} gCO₂/kWh"`, while Poland's coal-dominated grid produces `{python} f"{_ci_poland:.0f} gCO₂/kWh"`. The same model on the same hardware therefore carries a vastly different environmental cost.

### PUE: The Hidden Multiplier

Power Usage Effectiveness (PUE) measures how much energy the datacenter wastes on cooling and overhead. Quebec's typical PUE of `{python} f"{_pue_quebec:.2f}"` means `{python} f"{_ovh_quebec:.0f}%"` facility overhead, whereas Poland's typical PUE of `{python} f"{_pue_poland:.2f}"` means `{python} f"{_ovh_poland:.0f}%"` of IT energy is added for cooling and power delivery. Modern liquid-cooled facilities (`{python} f"{_pue_quebec:.2f}"`) are substantially more efficient than older air-cooled ones (`{python} f"{_pue_poland:.2f}"`).

### Connecting to TCO

Infrastructure specifications feed directly into both the `SustainabilityModel` (carbon and water footprint) and the `EconomicsModel` (electricity costs in TCO). Regional electricity prices vary as much as carbon intensity, a factor the TCO model accounts for.

### Cloud and storage pricing anchors

Illustrative list-price anchors for TCO analyses live under `Infrastructure.Pricing`:

```{python}
#| echo: true
gpu_hr = mlsysim.Infrastructure.Pricing.Cloud.GpuTrainingPerHour
egress = mlsysim.Infrastructure.Pricing.Cloud.EgressPerGB
s3 = mlsysim.Infrastructure.Pricing.Storage.S3StandardPerTbMonth

print(f"{gpu_hr.name}: {gpu_hr.rate:~P}")
print(f"{egress.name}: {egress.rate:~P}")
print(f"{s3.name}: {s3.rate:~P}")
```

Each `PricePoint` carries `metadata.provenance` pointing at the book economics appendix.

### Textbook Connection

The *Sustainable AI* chapter uses these grid profiles to quantify the carbon footprint of training runs. The *Compute Infrastructure* chapter connects PUE to total facility cost. Try the [Geography Tutorial](../tutorials/07_geography.qmd) to explore these tradeoffs interactively.
